level_cap_rule: `level=` calls Pokemon.setLevel, which fires no experience event, so rctmod's cap (an EXPERIENCE_GAINED_EVENT_PRE handler) never sees it and a set CAN overshoot the cap (note A2). The raise therefore writes exactly the cap it has just read into a score, and nothing else: no level is ever authored in this file
max_level_why: modpack/config/cobblemon/main.json maxPokemonLevel 100: the highest level a slot can hold, so the generated slot read tests levels 1..100
cooldown_why: a second submit of the same click (the dialogue can deliver one) must not buy twice: the ferry's per-player cooldown score, set only once the charge is about to be taken

price_rule.decision: the owner, 2026-10-21: service prices RISE WITH BADGES ('the iv/ev system costing 17k feels bad early game ... so far no one is doing optional fights just the gym trainers and leaders'), and 2026-10-22: 'make every change global, not just what players have done so far'. Built from docs/mechanics/ECONOMY_V3.md section 3.2 (its proposal_v3 numbers, unchanged at tiers 1-8) on 2026-10-22
price_rule.supersedes: the owner's decision (4) after the 2026-10-10 overnight ('a service is the convenience that costs more than the play it saves': one hour of the leg-8 fight hour, $17,200, EV from badge 2 and IV from badge 8). Kept below as superseded_price_rule; reversed for these three services by the 2026-10-21 choice
price_rule.rule: price(service, t) = the smallest multiple of round_to AT OR ABOVE fractions[service] x data/markets.json income_basis.path.leg_by_badges_held[t]: what the path (gym juniors, leaders, the eye-contact route and Victory Road trainers; tools/income_model.py) pays in the leg a player holding t badges is playing. tools/training_services.py audit refuses any price_by_tier that is not the rule's, so a re-measured income re-prices every tier
price_rule.fractions_why: a whole team (six EV spreads, thirty-six IV stats) bought across legs 2-5 lands near 55% of what the path pays by badge 5, leaving the rest for the Mart and one TM a leg (ECONOMY_V3.md 3.2 cash walk); six raises a leg cost 30% of the leg. Written as strings so the rule is exact (Fraction), not a float
price_rule.tiers_why: every badge count, 0 to 8 (the owner, 2026-10-22: global): tier 8 is a player holding eight badges, priced against Victory Road's ten (income_basis.path.leg_by_badges_held '8'), and after the Champion the raise stops at max_cap while EV and IV stay at tier 8

tier.raise: t = badges held (the raise writes the player's own cap)
tier.ev_and_iv: t = max(badges held, the slot's level band). The level band of a slot at level L is the smallest t whose cap_by_badges_held[t] >= L, else 8. So a high-level Pokemon traded to a low-badge friend is priced as the high tier it is (the co-op arbitrage a badge-only price opens)
tier.badges_held: the highest N whose advancement cobblers:flag/gymN_cleared the player holds (tools/progression_pack.py flags), 0 when none, read again in the function at every purchase; the dialogue shows each tier's price only to a player at that tier, by the same flags (compile_dialogue's flag/all/not conditions)

price_rule.cap_source: data/legendaries.json level_caps.upper_bound_by_badges 0..8 (the next leader's ace, then Lorelei's): tools/training_services.py audit fails if the two differ

superseded_price_rule.superseded_by: price_rule above (the owner, 2026-10-21: RISES WITH BADGES)
superseded_price_rule.decision: the owner, after the 2026-10-10 overnight (docs/STATE.md 'Owner decisions after the 2026-10-10 overnight' (4)): price the services and the craftables against each other, one way. Taken: CRAFTING (and training by battle) IS THE ROUTE; a service is the convenience that costs more than the play it saves. Reasoning and the numbers: docs/mechanics/SERVICES_AND_CRAFTING.md
superseded_price_rule.rule: a named service's price is the smallest multiple of round_to STRICTLY above hours_saved x the fight hour of anchor_badge's leg. The fight hour is data/markets.json income_basis.leg_by_badge[anchor_badge] / data/bank.json effort_model.max_leg_hours: the same exchange rate between an hour of play and money that R5 (effort_model.rules parity) already prices gathering against. tools/training_services.py audit refuses any other price, so a re-measured income re-prices the service

ev.why: ASSUMED, never timed (EXP timing replaces it): one Pokemon's two-stat spread by battle at a training ground is about 64 wild fights with a power item held (252 / 8 = 32 a stat, EV_IV_TRAINING.md 4.2), and by brewing it is 52 vitamins = 18 brewing-stand batches of three (one leek, one vivichoke, one EV berry a batch. The three steps medicinal_brew, pp_up and the vitamin are cobblemon:brewing_stand recipes read from Cobblemon-fabric-1.8.0+1.21.1.jar; that one ingredient serves three bottles is vanilla brewing-stand behaviour, ASSUMED to hold for Cobblemon's recipe type)

iv.why: ASSUMED: one stat's cap is a silver Bottle Cap plus eight mint leaves of that stat's colour (obc:bottle_cap_<stat>, read from Only Bottle Caps-1.5.0-fabric.jar). The silver cap is 3% of vanilla fishing treasure and 5% of Poke Rod treasure (obc-common.toml, measured); at vanilla's treasure share and cast time (ASSUMED) that is about 0.7 h with Luck of the Sea III and Lure III, about 3.5 h with a plain rod. One hour is the lower, enchanted figure

superseded_price_rule.kept_why: the hours-saved estimates are the only record of what each service saves; the shelf ordering they fed (a bought spread of vitamins or mochi costs more than the service) still holds at every tier

raise.price_why: price_rule, tier = badges held. Was a flat $500 (the owner's figure, 2026-10-09)
raise.gate_why: from the first cap (20) onward, the design's `From` column
raise.max_cap_why: ECONOMY_OVERHAUL.md section 5: a flat raise after the Champion (cap 100) would skip the arena's whole climb, so the flat service stops at cap 62. The recommended $200 a level above 62 is owner question 7 and NOT built: a player whose cap reads 63 or more is refused with nothing charged
refuses: the cap did not read (0): nothing is charged
the cap is above max_cap: nothing is charged
the slot is empty (no level 1..max_level matches): nothing is charged
the slot holds a Pokemon above the cap: nothing is charged
the slot is already at the cap: nothing is charged
the balance is short: nothing is charged
the charge did not take exactly the price: the service does nothing
the slot does not read back at the cap after the edit: the price is given back

ev.price_why: price_rule, tier = max(badges held, the slot's level band). Was $17,200 from badge 2 (superseded_price_rule)
ev.gate_why: open from the first cap, every tier priced (the owner, 2026-10-22: global, badges 0-8). Was gym2_cleared; ECONOMY_V3.md proposed gym1_cleared, and tier 0 is priced by the same rule so the first leg is not left out. Setting a flag here closes it again: the dialogue and the function both read services.ev.gate
ev.zero_why: EVs.canSet refuses a set that would pass 510 (note A1), and a set names only the stats it lists, so all six are zeroed in one command and the spread is set in a second; every spread below totals 508
ev.spreads_why: the design's `two stats to 252 and HP to 4`; where HP is one of the two, the 4 goes to the stat the spread most needs next
refuses: the slot is empty (no level 1..max_level matches): nothing is charged
the balance is short: nothing is charged
the charge did not take exactly the price: the service does nothing
ev.not_verified_after: the spread is not read back: whether testpartyslot matches <stat>_ev properties was not read from bytecode (note A1 covers level= and species= only), and a read-back that never matches would refund every purchase. EXP-062 S4 reads the EVs in the summary screen

iv.price_why: price_rule, tier = max(badges held, the slot's level band); all six cost six times a stat. Was $17,200 a stat from badge 8 only (superseded_price_rule)
iv.gate_why: open from the first cap, as the EV service (the owner, 2026-10-22: global). Was gym8_cleared
refuses: the slot is empty: nothing is charged
the balance is short: nothing is charged
the charge did not take exactly the price: the service does nothing
iv.repeat_rule: bought again at full price, even on a stat already at 31: the dialogue says so (ECONOMY_OVERHAUL.md section 5 `Limits`)
iv.not_verified_after: as the EV service: not read back (testpartyslot's IV matching is unread)

party_over_cap: NOT a refusal here, a deliberate departure from the design table's last clause: a raise writes exactly the cap, so it cannot put a party over it, and a party already over is told by tools/levelcap_pack.py's own notice. Checking it would make this pack call cobblers:levelcap/battle_check, and a `function` line naming a function another pack may not ship fails this pack's function at load
slot_choice: one dialogue page per service shows six options, Slot 1 to Slot 6; each runs its own small function (cobblers:training_services/<service>/.../slot<N>) that writes the slot into storage and calls the service's macro function with it. Cobblemon's dialogue `function` effect takes a bare function id (tools/compile_dialogue.py function_id), so the slot travels in the function's name, not in an argument. MoLang never chooses the slot

seat.why: two blocks east of the ground's sign (data/training_grounds.json sign.offset [0, 2]) so the keeper stands beside the sign that names the ground, off the Habitat Block's own column, on the heightmap's ground plus one, turned to face the town

messages.greeting: Want a shortcut? I train a Pokemon to your level cap, train in its effort, or perfect its stats. My prices rise with your badges.
messages.raise_option: Train a Pokemon to my cap (${raise_price})
messages.ev_option: Effort training (${ev_price} a Pokemon at your badges)
messages.iv_option: Perfect a stat (${iv_price} a stat at your badges)
messages.raise_page: Which one? I train it straight to your cap. Moves it would learn on the way are worth checking afterwards.
messages.ev_page: Pick a training plan. I clear what it had first, then train the plan in. A Pokemon above your badges' level costs the price of the badges its level needs.
messages.iv_page: Which stat? A stat already perfect costs the same: I do not check. A Pokemon above your badges' level costs the price of the badges its level needs.
messages.cap_unread: I can't read your level cap right now. Nothing was charged; try again in a moment.
messages.cap_closed: Your cap is past what I train to. Nothing was charged.
messages.slot_above_cap: That one is already above your cap. Nothing was charged.
messages.slot_at_cap: That one is already at your cap. Nothing was charged.
messages.slot_empty: There's no Pokemon in that slot. Nothing was charged.
messages.gated: Come back when you have {requirement}. Nothing was charged.
messages.short: That's ${price}, and you have ${balance}. Nothing was charged.
messages.charge_failed: The payment didn't go through, so I've done nothing.
messages.refunded: It didn't take. Your ${price} is back.

not_covered: the slot's moves and evolutions after a level set: setLevel fires no level-up event (note A2), so whether moves are learned or an evolution is offered is EXP-062 S2; the raise page warns the player
the slot's level is read by testing level=1..max_level one at a time (testpartyslot has no range syntax, note A1): up to 200 commands a purchase, well inside maxCommandChainLength
the postgame per-level price (owner question 7): not built
the keepers are placed by tools/reapply.py R17TS over RCON from this file; a world that has not run that step has no keepers
